newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares recover ground to end touch higher.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares recover ground to end touch higher.

text.p: Italian shares, which earlier moved lower dragged down by bond futures, recovered some ground by the close on Wednesday in the wake of a firmer Wall Street.
The all-share Mibtel index ended 0.17 percent up at 10,433 after a session low of 10,376.
But the Mib30 blue chip index closed down 0.05 percent at 15,625 with Olivetti and Fiat hit by profit-taking remaining weak, traders said.
"The tone of the market is still positive. There has been the inevitable profit-taking at the highs, but there were a few bullish spurts and some stocks have held up well," one trader said.
In fairly active business, traded volume was estimated at around 900 billion lire.

Olivetti, which gained some 30 percent in the last two weeks, closed 5.34 percent down at 550 lire after a low at 546 lire. Fiat closed 0.98 percent off at 4,540 lire as the market awaited developments of possible government moves to boost the sagging domestic car industry.

Telecoms had a good day, apart from Stet holding company which ended just 0.08 percent off at 6,275. Telecom Italia closed 1.21 percent up at 3,609 lire and mobile phone operator TIM ended 1.24 percent up at 3,435.
Energy giant ENI ended 0.23 percent up at 7,796 lire.
Banks were mixed, with Mediobanca, Banca Commerciale Italiana and Credito Italiano all posting losses but among gainers were Ambroveneto and Banca di Roma.
Insurances were also mixed with Alleanza, RAS and Toro firmer but Generali, INA, SAI and La Fondiaria all slipped.
